content.question: In Episode 2 the instructor introduced 'blending' while working with LinearLayout. What does 'blending' refer to in this context?

options.text: Using ConstraintLayout and blending constraints to overlap views.
Nesting layouts (e.g., putting a horizontal LinearLayout inside a vertical LinearLayout) to combine vertical and horizontal placements.
Applying a gradient background so two layouts visually blend together.
Using view animations to transition between different layout states.

content.explanation: Blending here means nesting layouts to achieve both vertical and horizontal arrangements—adding a horizontal LinearLayout inside a vertical one so some elements flow horizontally while others remain vertical.
hints: He said 'layout under layout' and added another LinearLayout.
It was demonstrated by setting orientation='horizontal' on a nested layout.
This was about arrangement, not visual effects.

content.question: Why did the instructor set the nested LinearLayout's height to wrap_content instead of match_parent when blending?

options.text: Because wrap_content reserves only the space needed for its children, preventing it from covering or pushing other components off the screen.
Because match_parent is deprecated for nested LinearLayouts and will throw an exception.
Because wrap_content automatically sets equal width among child views.
Because Android Studio forces using wrap_content in horizontal orientations.

content.explanation: He used wrap_content because he didn't know how many child elements would be placed; match_parent could cover other content and make it vanish. wrap_content adapts to children size.
hints: He warned that match_parent could make the above text vanish.
This is a layout behavior decision, not a tooling rule.

content.question: When placing image views inside the nested horizontal layout, which attribute did the instructor add to provide spacing between images?

options.text: android:padding='10dp' on the parent layout so children remain spaced.
android:margin='10dp' (or 5dp) on the ImageView elements to create outer spacing between them.
android:layout_weight='1' on every ImageView to distribute space.
Use a ShapeDrawable between images as a spacer view.

content.explanation: He added margin (5dp or 10dp) to ImageView elements to create gaps between them. Margin controls outer spacing between sibling views.
hints: He said 'add some margin into it. So margin, 5 dp margin will be good'.
Margin provides outside spacing between sibling views.
No weights or spacer drawables were used.

content.question: Which change would you make to allow a horizontal group of TextViews to appear side-by-side inside a vertical LinearLayout?

options.text: Set the parent LinearLayout to orientation='horizontal' and place all children directly inside it.
Nest a new LinearLayout with orientation='horizontal' inside the vertical parent and add the TextViews inside the nested layout.
Wrap each TextView inside a ConstraintLayout to force horizontal arrangement.
Set all TextViews to layout_width='0dp' without changing orientations.

content.explanation: Keep the outer container vertical and add a nested horizontal LinearLayout to host horizontally laid-out children. This mixes directions without affecting the rest of the screen.
hints: He used 'another linear layout' with orientation='horizontal'.
Goal: mix horizontal sections inside a vertical flow.

content.question: When creating a new activity the instructor mentioned the 'intent filter' in the manifest. What did he say about marking the activity as the launcher?

options.text: He insisted you must always mark new activities as launcher in the wizard; otherwise they won't compile.
He suggested you can set the intent filter later in the manifest and it's not mandatory to mark it as launcher during creation.
He recommended adding two launcher activities for redundancy.
He said launcher activities are deprecated and should not be used.

content.explanation: He noted you can place the intent filter later in the manifest file; there's no need to mark an activity as launcher during the new activity wizard if you don't want to.

content.question: Why did the instructor set the ImageView width and height to 100dp when demonstrating avatars?

options.text: To create a square avatar with consistent visual size (100dp × 100dp).
Because Android requires imageviews to be 100dp by default.
To make the ImageView automatically load a higher-resolution asset.
To prevent the ImageView from being clickable.

content.explanation: He set both width and height to 100dp to create a uniform square avatar size across the row.

content.question: What happens when you copy and paste a TextView inside a vertical LinearLayout in Android Studio, according to the instructor?

options.text: The pasted TextView appears directly below the previous one following the vertical stack behavior.
The pasted TextView overlaps the previous one and must be manually constrained.
The pasted TextView is placed at a random screen position.
The pasted TextView is converted into an ImageView automatically.

content.explanation: In a vertical LinearLayout each new child stacks below the previous — copy-paste follows this rule, so the pasted TextView appears below the original.

content.question: Why did the instructor avoid using match_parent on the nested horizontal LinearLayout?

options.text: match_parent would expand the nested layout and could cover other content, making the screen messy or hiding text above it.
match_parent is not allowed inside any LinearLayout and will cause a runtime error.
match_parent forces child views to use exactly 0dp width.
match_parent disables orientation on the nested layout.

content.explanation: Using match_parent could make the nested layout take all space and push or hide other components; that's why wrap_content was preferred.

content.question: The instructor used 'SRC' on ImageView to set an avatar resource. What does the 'src' attribute specify?

options.text: The image resource to display inside the ImageView (e.g., @drawable/avatar2).
The background color of the ImageView.
The layout width of the ImageView in dp.
The click listener method name for the ImageView.

content.explanation: The 'src' attribute sets the drawable resource displayed by the ImageView, such as an avatar image.

content.question: When the instructor deleted nodes while experimenting, what was his stated reason for using wrap_content on newly added layouts?

options.text: He used wrap_content because he didn't know how many elements would be placed and wanted the layout to size itself to children.
He used wrap_content because it enforces a minimum width of 300dp.
He used wrap_content because it disables margins automatically.
He used wrap_content because it makes components invisible until populated.

content.explanation: wrap_content ensures the container only uses the space needed by its children which is useful when the number or size of children is unknown.
